nodes.claim: For arbitrary fixed comparator u in V, R_T(u)=sum_t ell_t(x_t)-sum_t ell_t(u). Algorithm need not know u.

source.anchor: paragraph immediately below general Regret_T(u) display

nodes.claim: The book calls an algorithm no-regret when for every fixed u its regret is at most sublinear, writing lim_{T->infinity} R_T(u)/T <= 0. This is one-sided, not equality to zero.
R_T(u) also depends on the loss sequence, suppressed in notation.
At each t=1,...,T output x_t in V, pay ell_t(x_t), then receive loss feedback.

source.anchor: regret display and following adversarial-loss paragraph

nodes.claim: Losses may be adversarial. The metric is sum of losses against any comparator u in V, with convexity/bounded gradients as possible loss-class restrictions.
The source verbally interprets sublinear regret as average performance approaching that of any fixed strategy.
OCO means the loss functions are convex.
V is convex when lambda*x+(1-lambda)*y belongs to V for x,y in V and 0<lambda<1.
dom f={x in R^d : f(x)<+infinity}; used by the stated first-order convex inequality.
A function is convex when its epigraph is convex.
For f:R^d->(-infinity,+infinity] with convex domain, convexity iff f(lambda*x+(1-lambda)*y)<=lambda*f(x)+(1-lambda)*f(y), 0<lambda<1.
Composition with an affine transformation preserves convexity. Proof is left as an exercise in the continuation on print 11. This is available context, not an explicit citation inside Example 2.15.

source.anchor: Theorem 2.7 including Rockafellar 1970 Theorem 25.1 and Corollary 25.1.1

nodes.claim: If convex f:R^d->(-infinity,+infinity] is differentiable at x in int(dom f), then f(y)>=f(x)+<grad f(x),y-x> for every y in R^d.
For nonempty convex V, x* in V and f convex/differentiable on an open superset of V, x* minimizes f on V iff <grad f(x*),y-x*>>=0 for all y in V.
First-order convex lower bound plus nonnegative directional pairing imply f(y)>=f(x*) for all y in V.
If some feasible y has negative gradient pairing, segment z(alpha)=alpha*y+(1-alpha)*x* remains feasible and h(alpha)=f(z(alpha)) has h prime(0)<0, contradicting minimality for small positive alpha.
Nonempty closed convex V, x1 in V, eta_t>0. Output x_t, suffer convex loss differentiable on an open superset of V, set g_t=grad ell_t(x_t), update x_{t+1}=Pi_V(x_t-eta_t*g_t).
OGD moves against current gradient then projects; losses can be adversarial and need not be draws from a fixed distribution.
For nonempty closed convex V, Pi_V(x) is the unique nearest point. For y in V, ||Pi_V(x)-y||_2<=||x-y||_2.
Argmin of norm equals argmin of half squared norm; apply Theorem 2.8 to f(y)=||x-y||^2/2 to get <Pi_V(x)-x,y-Pi_V(x)>>=0.
Expand ||y-x||^2 around Pi_V(x) and discard nonnegative cross and square terms to obtain distance decrease.
eta_t*(ell_t(x_t)-ell_t(u)) <= eta_t*<g_t,x_t-u> <= (||x_t-u||^2-||x_{t+1}-u||^2)/2 + eta_t^2*||g_t||^2/2, for u in V and eta_t>0 under OGD assumptions.

source.anchor: Lemma 2.12 proof full display and reordering sentence

nodes.claim: Projection decrease and square expansion bound new-minus-old potential by -2*eta_t*<g_t,x_t-u>+eta_t^2*||g_t||^2, then convex linearization bounds loss difference.
For nonincreasing positive eta_t and diameter D, R_T(u)<=D^2/(2*eta_T)+sum eta_t*||g_t||^2/2-||x_{T+1}-u||^2/(2*eta_T). Retained as branch boundary, not applied to all-space Huber.

source.anchor: Theorem 2.13 Moreover statement and second display

nodes.claim: For eta_t=eta>0, every u in V satisfies R_T(u)<=||u-x1||^2/(2*eta)+(eta/2)*sum ||g_t||^2-||x_{T+1}-u||^2/(2*eta).
Divide Lemma 2.12 by positive eta_t and sum t=1,...,T.

source.anchor: first display block in Theorem 2.13 proof

nodes.claim: Reindex weighted potential differences; use nonincreasing eta_t to make reciprocal differences nonnegative, bound intermediate distances by D, and telescope reciprocal differences. Negative terminal term is retained.

source.anchor: second display block beginning In the same way

nodes.claim: For fixed eta all interior potentials cancel exactly, yielding initial distance minus terminal distance plus gradient-square sum. No diameter bound is used.
Constant-eta bound holds even when D=infinity and depends on initial distance to the comparator.
The last term in both bounds is nonpositive and usually discarded, though useful in advanced proofs.
Time-varying OGD on unbounded domains need not inherit the same guarantee; source points to Section 5.2 failure and Chapter 3 stochastic distinction.
Learning rates are chosen via regret analysis. The discussion chooses one constant learning rate for a fixed number of iterations.

source.anchor: opening optimization displays and two following paragraphs

nodes.claim: Formal minimizer eta=||u-x1||/sqrt(sum ||g_t||^2) would use unknown future gradients and comparator distance; adversarial data and dependence of gradients on eta prevent using this prescription generally. Future lower-bound/adaptive/parameter-free pointers are not proofs here.

source.anchor: paragraph beginning For the moment through Eq. (2.1)

nodes.claim: If ||g_t||<=L and bounded diameter D controls ||u-x1||, tune eta=D/(L*sqrt(T)) to get D*L*sqrt(T). Requires a bounded-diameter surrogate; not the route for V=R^d.

source.anchor: Example 2.15 opening through true price feedback

nodes.claim: z_t in R^d consists of past d opening prices and is available when predicting <z_t,x_t>. V=R^d. The true y_t is revealed after prediction.
The source calls Huber loss convex and robust to outliers, without proving convexity here.
nodes.evidence_snippet: a convex loss function robust to outliers

nodes.claim: With residual r=<z_t,x>-y_t: ell_t(x)=r^2/2 if |r|<=delta, else delta*(|r|-delta/2). Equality at threshold belongs to quadratic branch.
delta is the outlier threshold, switching from quadratic to linear error penalty. The text does not state delta>0 or delta>=0 explicitly.
Use OGD with constant learning rate eta proportional to 1/sqrt(T). Constant means within each horizon-T run.
grad ell_t(x)=r*z_t if |r|<=delta, else delta*sign(r)*z_t. The display includes the threshold equality in the first branch.
If all ||z_t||_2 are bounded, the gradients are bounded, so the assumptions of Theorem 2.13 are satisfied. No explicit numerical bound is printed.
Running OGD, on average algorithm performance approaches that of any fixed linear predictor. No exact Huber regret constant or limit formula is printed here.

source.anchor: Huber threshold paragraph and both piecewise displays

nodes.claim: Threshold sign is unstated. The intended convex Huber regime requires delta>=0, conventionally delta>0. delta=0 is a degenerate zero loss. Negative delta is not covered by the advertised convexity.

source.anchor: transition from loss display to gradient display

nodes.claim: The source supplies neither a proof of convexity of the scalar piecewise loss nor the join differentiability/chain-rule proof at residual +/-delta. These obligations are required to instantiate differentiable convex OGD.
The source omits the scalar-coefficient estimate and uniform quantifiers: for fixed delta>=0 and a common B>=0 with ||z_t||<=B, the displayed gradient has norm <=delta*B, uniformly in x,y_t,t.

For a quantitative/asymptotic statement one must specify eta=c/sqrt(T), c>0 fixed across T, and fixed initial x1 (or uniformly controlled initial distance). This is a known-horizon family of constant-step runs. The source does not specify c, an anytime construction, or initialization across runs.

The source omits substitution of the gradient bound into Theorem 2.13, division by T, and the one-sided limit/quantifier argument. Approach does not justify |R_T(u)|/T->0, equality to comparator loss, or uniform convergence over all u in unbounded R^d.

nodes.claim: Unique Euclidean projection on a nonempty closed convex set is asserted here without existence/uniqueness proof. It is an upstream omission in the cited general OGD chain, trivial for the Example domain R^d via the identity map.

routes.provenance: printed citation and supporting printed proof

root_proof_routes.note: Exactly one sufficient route is printed for Example 2.15. No second source route is invented. A second independently established sufficient route would be an OR sibling, never another mandatory AND conjunct.

non_routes.reason: V=R^d has no finite diameter for nontrivial d; Eq. (2.1) does not supply the Example bound.
Replacing eta=c/sqrt(T) within a fixed-T run by eta_t=c/sqrt(t) is an additional algorithm and needs a separate unbounded-domain analysis.
Future gradients and unknown comparator distance cannot set an admissible universal online stepsize.

assumption_ledger.item: d finite, Euclidean R^d, Euclidean inner product/norm
V=R^d; x1 in R^d; each u in R^d fixed over rounds
z_t known at prediction time; y_t revealed afterward
all feature norms uniformly bounded; no separate label bound
eta>0 constant within run; proportional to T^(-1/2)
fixed c>0, B, delta, u, x1 across T for displayed asymptotic adaptation
convexity, differentiability and numerical gradient estimate
no i.i.d., expectation, confidence event, stochastic filtration, bounded comparator ball or finite feasible diameter

derived_adaptations.assumptions: Intended delta>=0; ||z_t||<=B uniformly, B>=0; eta>0 constant; T>=1; arbitrary x1,u in R^d; Huber convexity/differentiability proved.
derived_adaptations.derivation: Use ||grad ell_t(x_t)||<=delta*B in the printed constant-step theorem. Original gradient-square-sum version can be stronger.

derived_adaptations.assumptions: Same as quantitative bound, with eta=c/sqrt(T), fixed c>0, and fixed delta,B,u,x1 as T varies. For each T rerun T steps with that eta.
derived_adaptations.derivation: Drop nonpositive terminal term and divide by positive T. This is pointwise in fixed u, not uniform over the unbounded comparator set and not an absolute-value or equality convergence statement.

genuine_unresolved_ambiguities: Threshold sign is implicit, with positive conventional and zero degenerate regimes distinct.
Proportionality constant and initialization across horizons are not specified.
Source verbal approach language and printed no-regret limit notation do not settle limit existence or two-sided convergence.
Exact detailed calculus proof and gradient-bound constant are omitted, not source-invalid by themselves.
